gloss: the curtain rises; to begin; to get underway

definitions.explanation: Literal use: the stage curtain goes up at the start of a play, concert, or similar performance.

definitions.gloss: to begin; to get underway; to open (of a major event or era)
definitions.explanation: Figurative use: a significant event, era, or contest begins — a tournament, a new political era, a project, a campaign. Carries a ceremonial or dramatic tone, framing the beginning as a public unfolding.

examples.japanese: {午後|ごご}7{時|じ}に{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる。
{会場|かいじょう}の{照明|しょうめい}が{落|お}ち、いよいよ{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The lights in the hall dimmed, and at last the curtain rose.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The curtain has risen on a new era.

examples.japanese: {選挙戦|せんきょせん}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The election campaign has gotten underway.

examples.japanese: {全国|ぜんこく}の{注目|ちゅうもく}を{集|あつ}める{大会|たいかい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がろうとしている。
examples.english: The tournament, which has drawn attention from all over the country, is about to get underway.

notes:
Literally 'the curtain goes up', referring to the rising of a stage curtain at the start of a performance. Widely used figuratively for the dramatic opening of any large event, contest, or era.

USAGE:
- The figurative use is much more common in writing and news than the literal theatrical use.
- Often takes a noun marked by の as its subject: {大会|たいかい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる, {新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる.
- Frequently appears with いよいよ ('at last'), ついに ('finally'), or ようやく for dramatic effect.
- The opposite is {幕|まく}が{下|お}りる ('the curtain falls') or {幕|まく}を{閉|と}じる ('to close; to come to an end'), used for conclusions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大会|たいかい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the tournament gets underway
- {新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: a new era begins
- いよいよ{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the curtain is about to rise at last
- {選挙戦|せんきょせん}の{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the election campaign gets underway

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幕|まく}が{下|お}りる: the curtain falls — the direct opposite, used when something ends.
- {幕|まく}を{開|あ}ける: to open the curtain; to begin an event — transitive counterpart; used when someone officially opens an event.
- {開幕|かいまく}する: to open; to start (of a season or event) — a more compact noun-verb with similar meaning; very common in sports reporting.
- {始|はじ}まる: to begin — the plain, everyday verb without the dramatic framing.
